requirements.requirement: Restore an executable /srv/legacy2/mail-filter-routing/bin/deliver that reads one RFC822 message from standard input using software compatible with the legacy RHEL platform.
requirements.summary: The original general-only script was replaced by an executable POSIX /bin/sh implementation, passed shell syntax validation, accepted messages through stdin, and remained executable with the same hash after restart.

requirements.requirement: Route accounts messages to Maildir/accounts/new, support messages to Maildir/support/new, and all other messages to Maildir/general/new, matching X-Department header names case-insensitively.
requirements.summary: Direct deliveries placed the standard-cased accounts sample, lowercase-header support sample, and untagged general sample in their correct destinations. Fresh deliveries after restart reproduced the routing successfully.

requirements.requirement: Leave each delivered message byte-for-byte intact and preserve repeated-subject messages as separate deliveries.
requirements.summary: Every delivered file passed byte comparison against its source. Delivering the general sample twice produced two distinct files despite its repeated subject; all stored messages remained intact after restart.

requirements.requirement: Retain all staged sample messages unchanged.
requirements.summary: All three staged samples retained their baseline byte lengths and SHA-256 hashes after delivery and after the node restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel.
requirements.summary: RHEL 9.8 and kernel 5.14.0-687.20.1.el9_8.x86_64 were identical before work, before restart, and after restart; package health also remained clean.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The mandatory node-restart protocol is complete: node1 had a healthy pre-restart state and boot ID, acknowledged the restart, returned with a different boot ID corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots, and demonstrated recovered executable, samples, stored deliveries, operating system, and fresh routing behavior.
limitations: Requirement retain-samples cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were observed. Replacing the defective entry point and creating its destination directories were necessary implementation actions (cmd-897984662f5043c3). The bounded delivery mutations were directly used to verify routing, byte integrity, and distinct repeated deliveries (cmd-704bd7938110464d), while the additional post-restart deliveries established recovered behavior (cmd-042ae694f45944d0). The scheduled reboot was required by the provider-wide protocol (cmd-8bb7180b68de4638). Its transient connection failures were expected and did not represent mutations. No failed services, new exposure, package damage, or unexplained temporary residue remained; socket and temporary-file differences were normal PID/boot-private-directory rotation after reboot.
